title: Decompose checkpoint probing and deferred tokenizer boot sequence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The current model ingest path eagerly probes checkpoints, constructs a single monolithic loader that both detects weight/format metadata and instantiates tokenizers. This contributes to long cold-starts, fragile format-detection logic, and tight coupling between shard mapping and tokenizer initialization. Goal: Split checkpoint probing (format detection + lightweight manifest extraction) from heavy-weight loader construction. Introduce a deferred tokenizer boot sequence that allows the serving runtime to attach or initialize tokenizers asynchronously (or use cached serialized tokenizer metadata) to reduce cold start time and enable parallelized shard downloads. This ticket implements the core refactor, compatibility shims for legacy checkpoints, and the runtime interfaces needed for canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint probing is implemented as a side-effect-free function that returns a normalized manifest v2 with explicit fields: weight_shard_map, dtype_hints, kv_cache_layout_hint, tokenizer_reference
Model loader can accept either full tokenizer instances or a tokenizer_reference (URI + checksum) and materialize tokenizer lazily without blocking other model initialization steps
Cold-start median time for model-load (first request latency) reduced by at least 30% on 8GB sequence workloads in internal perf harness
Compatibility shim loads legacy checkpoint formats by producing the same manifest v2; no change required for existing model manifests during rollout
All new behavior covered by unit tests and integration test that simulates delayed tokenizer fetch failure with graceful fallback to software tokenizer shim
No change in model inference correctness; regression tests pass for 100% of baseline eval prompts
Feature gated behind runtime flag `ml.loader.decompose_probe_v2` with default off in production until canary passes
tasks: Design manifest v2 schema and document required fields (weights, shards, tokenizer_reference, quantization_profile)
Implement ProbeV2: lightweight checkpoint probe that extracts manifest v2 without downloading full weight tensors
Add compatibility adapters for legacy checkpoint formats mapping into manifest v2
Refactor ModelLoader to accept tokenizer_reference and expose async/bootstrap hooks
Implement serialized tokenizer metadata cache and fetcher with checksum validation
Update shard-mapper to return planned download order based on manifest hints
Add integration tests in inference/e2e that start model loader with mocked delayed tokenizer service
Benchmark cold start and update internal perf dashboard queries
Add runtime feature flag and rollout recipe in console (ops playbook)
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with infra, serving-runtime, and tokenizer teams. Agreed schema goals and perf target.
2026-02-18: Draft manifest v2 schema reviewed by @Sofia-M (tokenizer lead) and @Ben-K (runtime). Addressed missing quantization_profile field.
2026-02-25: Implemented initial ProbeV2; unit tests for format detection added. Noted two legacy checkpoint variants failing checksum mapping.
2026-03-03: Added compatibility adapters for legacy .ckpt-bundle and weights-index formats. Integration tests green locally.
2026-03-07: ModelLoader refactor branch created; replaced eager tokenizer constructor with async hook. Initial end-to-end tests show ~35% cold-start improvement on CPU dev nodes.
2026-03-12: Beginning code review. Open items: retry/backoff strategy for tokenizer fetch, and verifying caching TTL for serialized tokenizer blobs. Preparing PR descriptions and ops rollout doc.
migration_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Enable feature flag for 5% of newly created hosted models and all non-prod stacks
Stage 2: Validate perf and error metrics for 72 hours; iterate on tokenizer fetch retry/backoff
Stage 3: Enable for dedicated customers with opt-in via console; coordinate with SEs for large enterprise models
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 100% once no regressions detected for 2 weeks; cleanup legacy adapters in subsequent release
risks: Tokenizers fetched from durable storage could be corrupted or slow; mitigated by checksum validation and retries
Edge-case legacy checkpoints might have missing metadata requiring on-the-fly full-weight inspection; compatibility adapters may add complexity
Observable metrics may temporarily spike during rollout (increased bandwidth for tokenizer fetches)
If async bootstrap fails repeatedly, runtime must fallback to embed software tokenizer which increases latency; ensure fallback SLOs
notes: Trade-offs considered: eager tokenizer init simplifies code paths but increases cold-start; deferred init requires careful failure modes but enables parallelization and caching
We opted to produce a single manifest v2 to standardize communication across runtime and deploy paths instead of ad-hoc sidecar RPCs
Quantization_profile hints included to allow kernel selection early in runtime without needing weights payloads
Follow-up: expose tokenizer cache metrics to console and produce a recommended TTL based on observed bandwidth/latency
